The vast majority of Americans search for information about loans while shopping online. As a result, speed and efficiency in the lending process are essential to all participants in the home-buying experience. Professionals need to use digital technology and automate procedures now so they can be competitive in the market. The average cost of processing a mortgage loan is more than $11,000. If lenders have inefficient or time-consuming processes, poor communication, or manual paperwork, it will tend to increase the processing cost and delay the date the customer receives their loan. By 2026, digital tools and mortgage automation will be a requirement for lenders to remain competitive. Research shows that the use of automated systems and loan processing software reduce error rates by almost 35%. Additionally, the average amount of time to close a loan can be significantly reduced with the implementation of digital workflows. This guide provides mortgage professionals with a variety of ways to improve their processes by implementing current technology and applying the principles of successful lenders. What is Loan Processing Efficiency? The level of efficiency with which lenders process loans is called loan processing efficiency. This refers to both the speed and the degree of accuracy with which a lender is able to move a mortgage from application to funding while keeping minimum costs. Efficiencies allow for fewer mistakes, quicker approvals, and greater ease of communication among loan officers, processors, underwriters, and borrowers. There are three primary factors that create efficiencies for lenders: Workflow automation: These systems will perform repetitive tasks automatically. Accurate data: The amount of erroneous data affects the likelihood of errors/faults occurring (generally referred to as rework). System integration: This will allow for seamless operation between all required systems and tools. By improving these three areas, lenders can process loans faster and at lower costs and provide their borrowers with a better customer experience in today’s crowded lending environment. The Mortgage Loan Processing Lifecycle (Where Inefficiencies Occur) The mortgage loan process consists of quite a few steps. Any inefficiencies at any one of these steps can cause delays in approvals and added costs. The main steps in the mortgage loan process are; lead generation, loan application (URLA 1003), loan processing, loan underwriting, loan closing and post-loan closing. There are several bottlenecks during the loan process that lenders will encounter. For example: Manual Data Entry Manually entering data causes lenders to have delays in processing the loan application. Manual Document Verifications The lender’s process to verify documents will require the lender to wait on documents that the borrower will be providing such as pay stubs and appraisals. While waiting on these documents can cause the lenders additional delays in processing their loans. Compliance Checks There may also be delays due to the compliance process not being automated. Lack of Communication Between Teams A lack of communication between departments will cause the lender to make multiple errors or result in having to redo the work. By identifying where there are delays throughout the lifecycle of the loan, lenders can focus on working to improve these areas. For example, how faster you can close a loan can be realized through using workflow automation at the application stage. Also, consider using technology for digital document management, building integrated communication tools for underwriting. Lenders who know the whole lifecycle and what is holding them up at every part of that cycle. Finding and fixing issues at all steps of your lending process will allow lenders to identify where the integration of systems will help them process loans more efficiently. If lenders don’t closely monitor post-closing workflows, they can reveal the bottlenecks that cause undue delay in processing. With loan workflow automation, lenders will be able to improve the speed of their loan operations while decreasing the number of errors made. Common Challenges in Loan Processing Mortgage lenders frequently experience similar obstacles when processing mortgage loans. Manual Workflows In manual processes, since lenders have less time to complete the loan approval process per loan, they have a higher tendency to make mistakes. Loan processors and officers spend a lot of time on these activities that do not add value to the lenders’ businesses. Therefore, lenders can increase productivity/efficiency by spending more time on high-value added activities. Poor Document Management If borrowers do not submit all required documents in an organized manner, this creates bottlenecks in the lenders’ workflow. In addition to wasting time, the process of gathering all of the necessary information will require lenders to reprocess those loans, causing significantly longer processing times. System Integration Gaps When there is not a fully integrated loan processing system, lenders must make multiple entries of data to the loan processing system. The lack of integration leads to more errors and increased processing time and significantly decreases the lenders’ visibility of all of their loans. Compliance Complexity There are many rules for the mortgage industry, including TRID, RESPA, and HMDA. These rules have additional steps that must be completed in any mortgage transaction workflow. Tracking compliance on a manual basis will increase an organization’s exposure to violating regulatory requirements. Communication and Collaboration Issues Internal team members do not communicate in an effective manner leading to miscommunication and delays. All team members must have a formalized assignment of tasks, be informed in a timely manner regarding tasks, and use methods for effective collaboration. Lenders that outperform their competitors in the marketplace have successfully addressed these issues by: Using an automated document workflow management system Utilizing a single repository to manage multiple independent systems that all have documents linked with them. Providing ongoing training for their employees related to loan processing software. As a result of addressing lenders’ issues effectively, operational costs per loan have been reduced by 40%-45%. Indeed, loan workflow automation lowers the amount of time to close a loan and enhances the borrower experience. Key Factors That Impact Loan Processing Efficiency Efficiency in the processing of a mortgage loan can be determined by four factors: Manual vs Automated Workflows By relying on manual processes, you are prolonging approval timelines and increasing your chances of making an error. When using Mortgage workflow automation, you can reduce processing time by 30% to 40%. This involves automating repetitive tasks such as requesting documents, sending alerts, and updating statuses. Data Accuracy and Upfront Validation Incorrect data about a borrower, or data that cannot be obtained (missing) leads to re-work, delays, and frustration. A mortgage processing software will improve the quality of the loan, which in turn will lead to quicker processing. System Integration Gaps Using disconnected tools, such as a pure CRM system, a LOS system, and an Appraisal system, create inefficiency by creating delays and requiring manual work. Proper API integrations allow all of the systems to talk to each other automatically, which makes processing faster and reduces errors. Compliance Complexity Mortgage loan regulations add another step to every loan that is processed. Manual compliance checks take a long time to complete and are prone to errors. By automating compliance tasks, staff will not have to perform verification of compliance rules. It eliminates additional burdens created by compliance. When lenders address these factors, they will be able to significantly improve their loan processing efficiency, reduce the number of errors, and create a more positive experience for borrowers. How to Improve Loan Processing Efficiency? (Top Strategies) To improve the efficiency of mortgage loan processing, there should be a combination of workflow design, technology, and team collaboration. Here are some of the five top strategies lenders will have access to: Automate Repetitive Tasks Automating repetitive tasks during the mortgage processing process can save time and help decrease the number of errors made by humans. Examples of these tasks include requesting documentation from borrowers and providing loan milestones to provide updates to borrowers. By using loan origination system implementation , lenders can combine multiple steps into one step by automating the tasks otherwise performed by employees. Consequently, the lender saves time in processing the loan by eliminating time lost in connecting with employees to complete the necessary paperwork. Implement Digital Document Management An eFolder cloud-based platform is designed to enable teams to electronically store all borrower documentation (i.e., the borrower’s application, payroll stubs, bank statements, etc.) in a central location. This enables lenders to track borrowers’ documentation electronically and manage them as if they were physical documents. The processing of transactions with electronic documents saved the lenders an estimated 40% of processing time. Use Automated Underwriting Early Using an automated underwriting system (AUS) early helps identify borrower eligibility issues prior to the processing of their loans. The use of an AUS provides an indication of how efficiently the lender will be able to provide a loan to the borrower. Hence, it reduces the chances of delays in processing from missing information and/or compliance errors. The use of an AUS provides timely feedback on the accuracy of the information provided by the borrower as compared to the type of loan the borrower is applying for. Hence, it increases the possibilities of providing the borrower with a loan quicker. Improve Borrower Data Collection Collecting accurate borrower data before the loan is created will help eliminate most of the communication back-and-forth and errors in the loan file. By creating an online portal or using structured forms, it helps the borrower provide all the required information on their first submission. In addition to improving operational efficiency, this action will impact business results. Quicker financing approvals will improve pull-through rates, and the ease of having a digital user experience will decrease application abandonment. Standardize Loan Workflows Utilizing consistent templates across the various types of loans, disclosures, and compliance will create consistency among our team. Consequently, creating standard processes relevant to mortgage loan processing will reduce the number of errors and will help speed up the approval process. Having standards in place will make it easier to train new employees. Enhance Team Collaboration To effectively process a loan, seamless communication must take place between loan officers (originators), processors and underwriters. Using the collaboration tools available within the LOS, teams will be able to work together more effectively and respond quickly to issues that may arise. Use Real-Time Pipeline Tracking Loan managers need to be able to see the real-time status of loans to locate loans that are moving forward toward closing or remain incomplete due to a delay. When the loan manager can identify potential problems at the beginning of the loan process, the loan manager will have the time to intervene to help keep the loan(s) moving from application to funding. Automate Document Collection and Borrower Intake Data entry errors and incorrect information creates significant delays within your business. Using manual document collection is the largest contributor towards delays in the loan origination process. Digitizing the collection of documents will substantially reduce inefficiencies caused by back-and-forth communication while providing accurate data from the beginning of the process. Integrate Core Systems (LOS, CRM and Other 3rd Party Tools) Lack of communication between systems is a leading cause of duplicate efforts and increased risk of errors. Loan origination systems must be integrated with other systems, including CRM systems, credit report and appraisal systems to minimize the need for manual data entry. Run Loans Through Automated Underwriting Systems Bottlenecks later in the loan process are typically caused by not processing loans through AUS early. By running loans through AUS early, you will be able to identify issues early in the process, reduce the number of times the same work is done (reworking) and accelerate loan approval times. This allows lenders to make quicker and more accurate lending decisions about whether to approve loans. As a result, the overall loan approval process times should be reduced. LOS can communicate with Credit Bureaus, Appraisers and Crm’s through the API Integration between them. By using this API Integration for automatic data transfer between the various systems allows lenders to have less manual data entry, errors and delays in processes. It also assists in determining the staffing level needed for their loan processing and how well they are performing throughout the loan cycle. With Predictive Analytics, lenders will have more effective planning to eliminate bottlenecks before they occur. Poor Document Management If borrowers do not submit all required documents in an organized manner, this creates bottlenecks in the lenders’ workflow. In addition to wasting time, the process of gathering all of the necessary information will require lenders to reprocess those loans, causing significantly longer processing times. System Integration Gaps When there is not a fully integrated loan processing system, lenders must make multiple entries of data to the loan processing system. The lack of integration leads to more errors and increased processing time and significantly decreases the lenders’ visibility of all of their loans. Compliance Complexity There are many rules for the mortgage industry, including TRID, RESPA, and HMDA. These rules have additional steps that must be completed in any mortgage transaction workflow. Tracking compliance on a manual basis will increase an organization’s exposure to violating regulatory requirements. Communication and Collaboration Issues Internal team members do not communicate in an effective manner leading to miscommunication and delays. All team members must have a formalized assignment of tasks, be informed in a timely manner regarding tasks, and use methods for effective collaboration. Lenders that outperform their competitors in the marketplace have successfully addressed these issues by: Using an automated document workflow management system Utilizing a single repository to manage multiple independent systems that all have documents linked with them. Providing ongoing training for their employees related to loan processing software. As a result of addressing lenders’ issues effectively, operational costs per loan have been reduced by 40%-45%. Indeed, loan workflow automation lowers the amount of time to close a loan and enhances the borrower experience.

sections.title: Key Factors That Impact Loan Processing Efficiency
sections.content: Efficiency in the processing of a mortgage loan can be determined by four factors: Manual vs Automated Workflows By relying on manual processes, you are prolonging approval timelines and increasing your chances of making an error. When using Mortgage workflow automation, you can reduce processing time by 30% to 40%. This involves automating repetitive tasks such as requesting documents, sending alerts, and updating statuses. Data Accuracy and Upfront Validation Incorrect data about a borrower, or data that cannot be obtained (missing) leads to re-work, delays, and frustration. A mortgage processing software will improve the quality of the loan, which in turn will lead to quicker processing. System Integration Gaps Using disconnected tools, such as a pure CRM system, a LOS system, and an Appraisal system, create inefficiency by creating delays and requiring manual work. Proper API integrations allow all of the systems to talk to each other automatically, which makes processing faster and reduces errors. Compliance Complexity Mortgage loan regulations add another step to every loan that is processed. Manual compliance checks take a long time to complete and are prone to errors. By automating compliance tasks, staff will not have to perform verification of compliance rules. It eliminates additional burdens created by compliance. When lenders address these factors, they will be able to significantly improve their loan processing efficiency, reduce the number of errors, and create a more positive experience for borrowers.

sections.title: How to Improve Loan Processing Efficiency? (Top Strategies)
sections.content: To improve the efficiency of mortgage loan processing, there should be a combination of workflow design, technology, and team collaboration. Here are some of the five top strategies lenders will have access to: Automate Repetitive Tasks Automating repetitive tasks during the mortgage processing process can save time and help decrease the number of errors made by humans. Examples of these tasks include requesting documentation from borrowers and providing loan milestones to provide updates to borrowers. By using loan origination system implementation , lenders can combine multiple steps into one step by automating the tasks otherwise performed by employees. Consequently, the lender saves time in processing the loan by eliminating time lost in connecting with employees to complete the necessary paperwork. Implement Digital Document Management An eFolder cloud-based platform is designed to enable teams to electronically store all borrower documentation (i.e., the borrower’s application, payroll stubs, bank statements, etc.) in a central location. This enables lenders to track borrowers’ documentation electronically and manage them as if they were physical documents. The processing of transactions with electronic documents saved the lenders an estimated 40% of processing time. Use Automated Underwriting Early Using an automated underwriting system (AUS) early helps identify borrower eligibility issues prior to the processing of their loans. The use of an AUS provides an indication of how efficiently the lender will be able to provide a loan to the borrower. Hence, it reduces the chances of delays in processing from missing information and/or compliance errors. The use of an AUS provides timely feedback on the accuracy of the information provided by the borrower as compared to the type of loan the borrower is applying for. Hence, it increases the possibilities of providing the borrower with a loan quicker. Improve Borrower Data Collection Collecting accurate borrower data before the loan is created will help eliminate most of the communication back-and-forth and errors in the loan file. By creating an online portal or using structured forms, it helps the borrower provide all the required information on their first submission. In addition to improving operational efficiency, this action will impact business results. Quicker financing approvals will improve pull-through rates, and the ease of having a digital user experience will decrease application abandonment. Standardize Loan Workflows Utilizing consistent templates across the various types of loans, disclosures, and compliance will create consistency among our team. Consequently, creating standard processes relevant to mortgage loan processing will reduce the number of errors and will help speed up the approval process. Having standards in place will make it easier to train new employees. Enhance Team Collaboration To effectively process a loan, seamless communication must take place between loan officers (originators), processors and underwriters. Using the collaboration tools available within the LOS, teams will be able to work together more effectively and respond quickly to issues that may arise. Use Real-Time Pipeline Tracking Loan managers need to be able to see the real-time status of loans to locate loans that are moving forward toward closing or remain incomplete due to a delay. When the loan manager can identify potential problems at the beginning of the loan process, the loan manager will have the time to intervene to help keep the loan(s) moving from application to funding. Automate Document Collection and Borrower Intake Data entry errors and incorrect information creates significant delays within your business. Using manual document collection is the largest contributor towards delays in the loan origination process. Digitizing the collection of documents will substantially reduce inefficiencies caused by back-and-forth communication while providing accurate data from the beginning of the process. Integrate Core Systems (LOS, CRM and Other 3rd Party Tools) Lack of communication between systems is a leading cause of duplicate efforts and increased risk of errors. Loan origination systems must be integrated with other systems, including CRM systems, credit report and appraisal systems to minimize the need for manual data entry. Run Loans Through Automated Underwriting Systems Bottlenecks later in the loan process are typically caused by not processing loans through AUS early. By running loans through AUS early, you will be able to identify issues early in the process, reduce the number of times the same work is done (reworking) and accelerate loan approval times. How This Impacts Each Role Loan officers → faster pre-qualifications Processors → less document chasing Underwriters → cleaner files Managers → better visibility
